(1) the cross sections of the heaviest isotopes in the xn–evaporation channel are predicted to be σ x n ≃ ( 1 − 10 ) fb, (2) the production cross sections of the most exotic isotopes in the pxn–evaporation mode can be σ p x n ∼ ( 10 − 100 ) fb, and (3) the cross sections for the production of the heaviest superheavy isotopes with Z=112−118
in the 48Ca + 238 U reaction, for the production of the isotopes 112-118, it is possible to use the xn, pxn, αxn channels.
in the 1–3n evaporation channels of the reactions 48 Ca + 208 Pb and 48 Ca + Th isotopes with Z=112, 114, 116, 118 and A=278–282 can be synthesized directly in reactions with emission 1–3 neutrons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibilities of direct production of the heaviest superheavy nuclei in the xn–evaporation channels, and with the possibilities of their synthesis in the pxn– and α xn–evaporation reactions.
the synthesis possibilities of new isotopes in the reactions 48Ca + 238U, 248Cm, 249Bk, 254Es and 254Fm.
the synthesis of superheavy nuclei in the 48 Ca+ 238 U reaction with the emission of 3–6 neutrons and the emission of protons and/or alphas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 48Ca+ 244Pu, 48Ca+248Cm, and 48Ca+249Bk reactions are very promising to synthesize new superheavy nuclei in the 1–2n–evpaporation channels.
the production of superheavy elements in reactions with the 48 Ca projectile is very promising.
the production of new superheavy nuclei in reactions of 48Ca with 208Pb, 232Th and 238U targets is possible in the α xn–evaporation channels with cross sections in the 50–500 fb range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of the isotopes with Z=112-118 in the 1p1n-, 1p2n-, 1n-, 2n-, 3n- and 4n-evaporation channels is possible.

the production cross sections in different evaporation modes are calculated for 48 Ca-induced reactions on actinides and the synthesis of new superheavies in the 1–4n–evaporation, p x n –, and α x n –evaporation channels is predicted.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the production cross sections of superheavy elements can be predicted with high accuracy, and that the production of the heaviest isotopes in superheavy elements can occur in the 1–2 n –evaporation channels.
the production of new superheavy nuclei in the 1 n – and 2 n –evaporation channels of complete fusion reactions with 48 Ca ions is possible.
the synthesis of new isotopes in the α xn–channel can be a promising way to extend the known isotopic chart of superheavy nuclei.
